subject.title: [Bug] Session flush blocks write tool completely during compaction

question: Should memory-triggered compaction runs continue to have single-target append-only write authority, or may they pass through unrelated non-memory writes under the normal workspace/sandbox write policy?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes a silent housekeeping run's write authority and current policy treats this as a security/product boundary, not a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Keep single-target guard
options.body: Leave memory-triggered runs restricted to the daily memory file and accept that unrelated writes must wait until the flush completes.

options.title: Allow narrow non-memory passthrough
options.body: Permit writes outside the memory-flush target only after normal workspace/sandbox validation, with regression tests and docs that define the exception.

options.title: Design explicit override
options.body: Add a deliberate user/operator-controlled unlock or config mode instead of changing default memory-run authority.

recommendation.title: Allow narrow non-memory passthrough
recommendation.body: Permit writes outside the memory-flush target only after normal workspace/sandbox validation, with regression tests and docs that define the exception.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged history for the current strict memory-flush guard and path-forwarding behavior points to frankekn-authored PRs.
